title: Inertia of a pair bound through a field of oscillator cells

key_results.statement: Bands $\varepsilon_i=\sigma_i\sqrt{\bar M_i^2+\tau^2\sin^2p}$ of the bodies at first order in the grip, signed inertias $I_i=\sigma_i\bar a M_{k_i}/\tau^2$ with $\bar a=F_0+F_2w_0$, form factor $\sigma_i\cos\frac{\theta_i(p)+\theta_i(p')}{2}$ of the grip between band states; minima of $E_i$ at $p=0$ and $p=\pi$.

Mutual term at second order in $\delta F$: $-\frac{\mu_1\mu_2c_1c_2}{2L}\sum_j[F_1^2/(\omega_q^2-\Delta_j^2)+\frac{F_2^2}{L}\sum_{a+b=q}\Omega_{ab}/(\omega_a\omega_b(\Omega_{ab}^2-\Delta_j^2))]$ between labels $(p_1,p_2)\to(p_1-q,p_2+q)$, valid for every label when $r\min(1,\lambda_{C,i}/2)\le1$.

Effective joint contract in the sector $P$: $\varepsilon_1(p_1)+\varepsilon_2(p_2)+U$, up to single-body self-energies and $O(\delta F^3)$ (terms $\propto F_1^2F_2$, $F_2^3$, relative order $u$; $O(\delta F^4)$ for $F_2=0$).

Time representation $U=-c_1c_2\int_0^\infty\frac12\sum_j\cosh(\Delta_jt)W(r,t)dt$, $W=2\mu_1\mu_2[F_1^2\Gamma_r+2F_2^2\Gamma_r^2]$; for held bodies it is the static bond (2.11) in (G2), of the sign of $-\mu_1\mu_2$ at every separation.
Bond of a pair moving with $V=P/I$: $U_P=U+V^2[-U/\tau^2+(rU)'/(2c_0^2)]$ at second order in the velocities, for $\ell\gg1$, relative corrections $O(\ell^{-2},a_b^{-2},\lambda_C^2/a_b^2)$.

One-quantum moving bond at order $V^2$: below the pinning length constant and slope change by $1-V^2(\tau^{-2}-\frac12c_0^{-2})$ and $1-V^2(\tau^{-2}-c_0^{-2})$; above it the range is $\ell\sqrt{1-V^2/c_0^2}$.

A bound level near labels 0 exists for branches $(+,+)$ (lowest level), for mixed branches iff the member in branch $+$ has the larger $\bar M$ (highest level), never for $(-,-)$; the extreme level is the even combination of two valley copies, unique for $t\neq0$.

Deep regime $1,\lambda_C\ll a_b\ll\ell$ with $\epsilon_J=\frac{2F_2^2}{\pi F_1^2c_0}\ln\frac{\ell}{a_b}\ll1$ (grips with $\epsilon_J$ not small excluded): $\Delta E=U(0)+\alpha(\lambda^2/2m_{\rm red})^{1/3}$, $\langle T\rangle=\frac\alpha3(\lambda^2/2m_{\rm red})^{1/3}$, $\lambda=\mu_1\mu_2F_1^2/(2c_0^2)$, relative corrections $O(a_b/\ell,\epsilon_J)$; shallow regime $a_b\gg\ell$: $\Delta E=-m_{\rm red}g^2/2=-\langle T\rangle$, $g=-\sum_rU(r)$; in the range (N) of (7.15), ordinary coefficients in (I) and formal coefficients outside (I).

$E_b(P)=E_b(0)+P^2/(2I_{\rm pair})+O(P^4)$, $I_{\rm pair}=I_1+I_2+D$, $D=3\langle T\rangle/\tau^2+2\langle U\rangle/\tau^2-\langle(rU)'\rangle/c_0^2+4I_1I_2\langle T\rangle$ (members, form factor, retardation, lattice), at first order in $|\Delta E|/\bar M$; $I_i=\sigma_i\bar M_i/\tau^2+I_i^{(2)}$ of the bodies dressed alone, $I_i^{(2)}$ cancels from $D$ and the members' own second-order terms enter $D$ at relative order $\delta F^2$; in the range (N) of (7.15), formal coefficients outside (I).

$D=[(2-r^2)\Delta E+(1-r^2)\langle T\rangle]/\tau^2+4I_1I_2\langle T\rangle$ in the continuum regime, at first order in $|\Delta E|/\bar M$; in the range (N) of (7.15), formal coefficient outside (I).

Deep (with $\epsilon_J\ll1$): $D=(2-r^2)\Delta E/\tau^2+O((1+\lambda_{C,1}^{-1}\lambda_{C,2}^{-1})\frac{a_b}{\ell}\frac{|\Delta E|}{\tau^2})$, leading only for $a_b\ll\ell\min(1,\lambda_{C,1}\lambda_{C,2})$; shallow: $D=\Delta E(\tau^{-2}-4I_1I_2)[1+O(\ell/a_b)]$, lattice-dominated with the sign of $-\Delta E$ for $(+,+)$, $r<2$ in the heavy range, and $D=\frac{\Delta E}{\tau^2}[1+O(\ell/a_b,(r\ell)^{-2})]$ in the light range with $r\ell\gg1$; in the light range with $r\ell$ not large ((I) included) the $r^2$ terms are $O(\ell^{-2})$, $\lambda_{C,i}$ is bounded only from below ($\lambda_{C,i}>2r\ell$), and the lattice part is at most $|\rho|/(r\ell)^2$ times $|\Delta E|/\tau^2$ and can be of order one.

With (7.10) at every binding strength, at fixed levels $D=\Delta E/v^2$ with one speed iff $r^2=1+4\sigma_1\sigma_2/(\lambda_{C,1}\lambda_{C,2})$, $v=\tau/\sqrt{2-r^2}$, impossible for $(+,+)$ under (D), for mixed branches $\lambda_{C,1}\lambda_{C,2}=4/(1-r^2)$ with $r<1$, outside the light range whenever $1-r^2\ge(r\ell)^{-2}$ and reached in (I); at leading order in every part of (N) where the regime exists: $v=\tau/\sqrt{2-r^2}$ deep with $a_b\ll\ell\min(1,\lambda_{C,1}\lambda_{C,2})$ (none for $r\ge\sqrt2$), $v=\tau(1-4\sigma_1\sigma_2/(\lambda_{C,1}\lambda_{C,2}))^{-1/2}$ shallow where real, coinciding iff the condition holds; heavy range (formal): $v=\tau=c_0$ at $r=1$ deep, no real shallow speed for $(+,+)$ at $r<2$; light range with $r\ell\gg1$ (formal): $v=\tau$ up to $O((1-r^2)\ell/a_b,(r\ell)^{-2})$ for every binding strength at $r$ of order one, $v=\tau=c_0$ at $r=1$; light range with $r\ell$ not large (isolated range (I), $r<1/(2\ell)$, with ordinary coefficients, formal otherwise): $v=\tau/\sqrt2$ deep up to $O(\ell^{-2})$ and $\tau(1-4\sigma_1\sigma_2/(\lambda_{C,1}\lambda_{C,2}))^{-1/2}$ shallow, so the speed depends on the binding except for mixed branches at $\lambda_{C,1}\lambda_{C,2}=4/(1-r^2)$, where $v=\tau/\sqrt{2-r^2}$ for every binding strength (such levels occur in (I) and, with formal coefficients, in the light range outside (I)).

Contribution of the mutual term to the fall: $\frac{w_{\rm pair}/I_{\rm pair}}{w_i/I_i}-1=\frac{w_b/\kappa-D}{I_1+I_2}=[(s-2+r^2)\langle U\rangle-(4-2r^2+4\tau^2I_1I_2)\langle T\rangle]/(\sigma_1\bar M_1+\sigma_2\bar M_2)$, $s=4F_0F_2/F_1^2$, $\kappa=F_1\tau^2/\bar a$ the members' ratio at first order in the grip, at leading order in the grip and first order in $\Delta E/\bar M$, in the range (N) of (7.15), for $a_b\ll\ell$ (the made field of a distant source varies on $\ell$ on the pinned ring); the variation over the pair enters at $O((a_b/\ell)^2|\Delta E|/\bar M)$.

In the range (N), in the deep regime (the only one with $a_b\ll\ell$), the pair falls like its members at first order in the grip ($w_b=\kappa D$) iff $s=2-r^2$, at leading order in $a_b/\ell$, $a_b/(\ell\lambda_{C,1}\lambda_{C,2})$ and $\epsilon_J$ (square grip: iff $r=1$, reached only in the heavy range with $a_b\ll\ell\lambda_{C,1}\lambda_{C,2}$, formal coefficients; linear grip: iff $r=\sqrt2$); in (I) neither grip meets it; a comparison with the dressed members needs their second-order weights and inertias, which change $w_i/I_i$ at the order of (7.13), and a common dressed ratio.

A member in branch $+$ at label 0 cannot decay with one or two quanta at second order iff $\bar M_i>\Omega_{\max}/2$ ($F_2=0$) or $\bar M_i>\Omega_{\max}$ ($F_2\neq0$) (heavy range; it implies $\lambda_{C,i}<r$, resp. $<r/2$), or $\bar M_i<\min_q[\omega_q-E_i(q)]$ (light range; it implies $\bar M_i<m_h/2$, and it is empty for $r>1$ with $(r^2-1)/r\ge1/\ell$); a bound level is an isolated eigenvalue iff $\sigma_1\bar M_1+\sigma_2\bar M_2+\Delta E<m_h-\sqrt{\bar M_1^2+\tau^2}-\sqrt{\bar M_2^2+\tau^2}$ (range (I)), which lies in the light range and needs $r<1/(2\ell)$, so no level of the heavy range is isolated.

open_issues: Third-order terms of the elimination (∝F₁²F₂, F₂³), fourth-order terms and single-body self-energies are not computed; argued small by u, r²|U(0)|/M̄ and δF²; the code checks only the second-order effective contract.
Deep bound levels of grips with ε_J not small (two-quantum bond dominant near r=0) are excluded, not treated.

Outside the range (I) of (7.15) the coefficients of items 2 and 3 are formal coefficients and the widths (fourth or higher order in δF) are not computed; isolated levels need r<1/(2ℓ), so r=1 is reached only by formal coefficients; code check (ii) uses members of the heavy range only.
Mixed-branch bound level: extra condition ΔE<γ and exclusion M̄1≈M̄2.
Bound levels of (−,−) near labels ±π/2 (out of scope by the note of the question) and bound levels outside the continuum regime are not treated.
Item 3 is answered only for a_b≪ℓ (deep regime); shallow pairs are not treated; the fall is compared with the members at first order in the grip, not with the dressed members (06-mark-inertia).
Only the ring; the cubic torus is a later package.
